title: Imaging Hydrogen, Its 3D Inhomogeneity and Strain Mapping of Palladium Hydride (PdH) Nanoparticle Catalyst by Ptychography
content: Metal hydrides are important in hydrogen storage, catalysis and energy conversion technologies, where their performance is closely linked to the nanoscale distribution of hydrogen [1, 2]. Unlike bulk metal hydrides, nanostructured hydrides exhibit unique hydrogen occupancy patterns due to size effects, and strain-induced variations [3, 4]. To understand how to optimize their industrial functionality, it is essential to resolve hydrogen distribution at the atomic scale. However, direct imaging of hydrogen in metal hydride nanoparticles remains highly challenging due to its weak electron scattering cross-section.
